JUDGMENT

The petitioners have filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act seeking Compensation of Rs.55,00,000/ for the death of one Smt. Roopavathi J. in a road traffic accident dated 09.02.2021.
2.

The case of the Petitioners in brief is that, SCCH-25 On 09.02.2021 at about 5.30pm, the deceased herein namely Roopavathi J was going towards Vemagal from Kolar by travelling in a Suzuki Access Scooter bearing Reg.No.KA 07EB6581 as a pillion rider ridden by one Venkateshappa.

When they reached near Chunchadenahalli gate on Kolar Narasapura NH75 Road, Kolar Taluk, a Goods Tempo bearing Reg.No.KA05AH9979 came from same direction,
driven by its driver with high speed in a rash and negligent manner, endangering human life, lost control over his vehicle went to its wrong side and dashed violently against the said scooter.
Due to impact deceased fell down and suffered grievous injuries.

3. It is the further case of the petitioners that, immediately after the accident the deceased was shifted to R.L.Jalappa Hospital, Kolar, provided first aid and thereafter shifted to Baptist Hospital,
Bangalore wherein she succumbed to the injuries on the same day during the course of treatment.
At the time of the accident, the deceased was SCCH-25 aged about 44 years, hale and healthy, working as a Teacher at Seventh Day Adventist School, KGF and earning Rs.18,000/ per month.

Due to sudden demise of Smt. Roopavathi J., the petitioners suffered mental shock and agony, Pain,
disappointment, anguish, frustration, loss of love etc.,
The petitioners have further claimed that they have spent Rs.2,00,000/ towards treatment, medicine, transportation and funeral obsequies.
The accident occurred due to the negligence of the driver of the Goods Tempo.
The Kolar Rural Police have registered a case against him in Cr.No.44/2021.
The 1st respondent being the RC owner and the 2nd respondent being the Insurer of the said offending vehicle jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners.
Hence, this petition.
4. In response to the summons issued by this court, the Respondent No.2 appeared and filed written statement.
In spite of due service of summons respondent No.1 did not appear and hence, placed exparte.

sentences.text:
2 5. The objections of the Respondent No.2:
It has stated that, there was non compliance of Sec.134(c) and 158(6) of the MV Act.
The driver of the Goods Tempo did not have valid and effective DL as on the time of the accident.
Further the vehicle is also not having valid permit to ply on the road.
The accident is due to the negligence of the rider of the motorcycle.
The police filed false charge sheet against the driver of the Goods tempo colluding with the claimants and owner of the vehicle.
Further denied the nature of accident, age, income and avocation of the deceased and contended that the compensation claimed by the petitioners is highly exorbitant.
Hence prays for dismissal of the petition.

6. On the above rival contentions of the parties, this court had framed the following issues:
1.

Whether the Petitioners prove that, they are the legal heirs of the deceased Smt.
Roopavathi J.?
SCCH-25 2.

Whether the Petitioners prove that, Smt. Roopavathi J. died on account of road traffic accident took place near Chunchadenahalli Gate, on Kolar - Narasapura NH75 Road, Kolar Taluk & District, due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of Goods Tempo vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA05AH9979, dated 09.02.2021 at about 5.30pm?
3. Whether the Petitioners are entitled for compensation? If so, what is the quantum?

From whom?
4

. What Order or Award?
7.
In order to prove their case, the Petitioners have examined 1st petitioner as PW.1 and got marked 11 documents as per Exs.P.1 to 11.
On the other side the Respondents did not examine any witness nor produced any document.

8. Heard both Counsels and perused the materials on record.
9.

My finding to the above issues are as follows: SCCH-25 Issue No.1 : In the affirmative Issue Nos.2 & 3 : In the affirmative, Issue No.4 : As per final order for the Following:
REASONS 10. Issue No.1:
In order to prove that the petitioners are the legal heirs of the deceased, the petitioner No.1 got examined himself as PW.1 and has reiterated about the relationship in his affidavit in chief.
In addition he got marked notarized copies of Adhar Cards of the petitioners and the deceased as per Ex.P.11.

According to Ex.P.11, both the petitioner Nos.2 & 3's father's name is mentioned as P. Vijay Kumar and in the Aadhar Card of the deceased, her husband's name is P. Vijay Kumar vs Lakshmi Venkateshwara Enterprises on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/6745026/
3 mentioned as P.Vijay Kumar.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: According to Ex.P.11 petitioner Nos.1 to 3 are the husband and children of the deceased.
Therefore, the Tribunal holds that the petitioner Nos.1 to 3 are the husband and children of the deceased Roopavathi J.
Accordingly, Issue No.1 is held in the affirmative.
SCCH-25 11. Issue No.2

: The Petitioners, to prove that the accident occurred due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the Goods Tempo have examined First Petitioner/Husband of the deceased as PW.1 and got marked Exs.P.1 to 10.
PW.1 has reiterated the averments of the petition in his affidavit filed in lieu of his chief examination.
During the cross examination of PW.1, nothing worthwhile is elicited.
12. The FIR was registered on the same day as per Ex.P.1 and the charge sheet is also filed by the police as per Ex.P.10.
As per the sketch at Ex.P.6 it can be seen that it is NH75 Road, there was a road divider near the accident spot.

According to Ex.P.7, there was damage to the left side head light, front bumper and bonnet on left side of the Goods Tempo and there was damage to the handle bar, right side rear foot rest and right side rear body pressed and damaged to the motorcycle.
The respondents have not led any contrary evidence.

Therefore, on the basis of the documents before the SCCH-25 court it is clear that the accident occurred due to the negligence of the driver of the Goods Tempo and the deceased Roopavathi J. died as per the report at Exs.P.8 & 9 i.e., Inqeust Mahazar and PM report.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 in the affirmative.
13. Issue No. 3: PW.1 to prove the income of the deceased has not produced any documents like appointment order, pay slips and Bank statement nor examined her employer.
The accident occurred in the year 2021.
Therefore, this court deems it fit to consider notional income at Rs.15,000/ per month.
Age of the deceased 14.
In so far as age of the deceased is concerned, the Petitioners have produced notarized copy of Aadhar Card of the deceased as per Ex.P.11.
This is a public document and has got presumptive value under law.
As per said document, SCCH-25 the date of birth of the deceased was 15.12.1976 and the accident occurred on 09.02.2021.
As such, the age of the deceased is 45 years as on the date of accident.
(i) LOSS OF DEPENDENCY AND FUTURE  PROSPECTS:

As per the principles of law laid down in the case of Sarla Verma V/s Delhi Transport Corporation,
appropriate multiplier applicable to her age is 14.

Since the sons are major, they are not considered as the dependents of the deceased.
However the petitioner No.1 is an Agriculturist in which the income varies.

Therefore,

sentences.text: 15. As per the decision of Hon'ble Supreme court in National Insurance company Vs Pranay Sethi and others SCCH-25 (AIR 2017 S.C 5157) persons aged about above 60 years are not entitled to any future prospects.

entities.text: National Insurance company Vs Pranay Sethi and others SCCH-25 (AIR 2017 S.C 5157)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
As mentioned above, since the deceased comes between 40 to 50 years age slab,
25% future prospects is to be added to her monthly income.

So Rs.3,750/ (Rs.15,000/ X 25% =
Rs.3,750/) should be added to her monthly salary of Rs.15,000/ then it comes to Rs.18,750/ per month.
As per the Sarala Verma case, if there is a sole dependent then  of the deceased income has to be deducted towards her personal and living expenses.

Then, the balance comes to Rs.9,375/
(Rs.18,750/  Rs.9,375/).

Therefore, the total loss of dependency would be Rs.15,75,000/
(Rs.9,375/ X 14 x 12) = Rs.15,75,000/).
i) LOSS OF CONSORTIUM:

In Magma General Insurance company Limited Vs. Nanuram (2018)
18 SCC 130

18 SCC 130
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: , the Hon'ble Apex court has observed "Consortium" is a compendious term, which SCCH-25 encompasses spousal consortium, parental consortium and filial consortium.
The right to consortium would include the company, care, help, comfort, guidance, solace and affection of the deceased, which is a loss to her family.
With respect to a spouse, it would include sexual relations with the deceased spouse".

16. This observation of the Hon'ble Supreme Court is reaffirmed in United Indian Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Satinder Kaur @ Satvinder Kaur and others, (2021) 11 SCC 780.
17.

sentences.text: The Petitioner Nos.1 to 3 are the husband and children who have lost their loving and care taking wife and mother at the age of 59, 24 and 19 years respectively and they have to the live remaining part of their life without her.

They are entitled to a sum of Rs.44,000/ each, in total Rs.1,32,000/
is awarded under the head of loss of consortium.
SCCH-25  i) TRANSPORTATION AND FUNERAL  EXPENSES:
PW.1/Petitioner No.1 has stated that he has spent Rs.2,00,000/ towards funeral expenses and obsequies etc..
In this regard he has not produced any bills pertaining to the above said expenses.
However, there are expenses during the death of a person for which documents cannot be maintained.

Therefore, in the interest of justice, the Petitioner is awarded a sum of Rs.20,000/
under this head.
ii) LOSS OF ESTATE:
As mentioned above, the deceased was earning a sum of Rs.18,000/ per month.
Out of this, she would have saved some amount and created estate in favor of the Petitioners.
Therefore, the Petitioner is entitled to a sum of Rs.20,000/ under the head of loss of estate.

As such, in total, the Petitioners are entitled to a sum of Rs.17,47,000/.

5 SCCH-25 LIABILITY 18.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: During the cross examination of PW.1 he has stated that he does not know the status of the MVC No.186/2021 filed by him in Kolar Court.
When the Tribunal check the same in CIS, it was found that the same was dismissed due to this case.
The respondent No.2 has contended that there was negligence on the part of the rider of the scooter.
But it has not proved the same.
Therefore, the respondents No.1 & 2 being the RC owner and the insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the said compensation to the Petitioners and satisfy the award.
Though the Petitioners claimed compensation of Rs.55,00,000, Petitioners are entitled only for a sum of Rs.17,47,000/ with interest @ 6% per annum.
Therefore, the petition needs to be allowed in part.
Accordingly I answer Issue No.3 in the affirmative.
SCCH-25 19. Issue No.4: For the reasons and discussions made above and finding to the above issues, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following: ORDER
The Petition filed by the Petitioners under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby allowed with cost.

The Petitioners are entitled for  Compensation of Rs.17,47,000/ (Rupees Seventeen Lakhs Forty Seven Thousand only) along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of Petition till the date of deposit of the Award amount.
The Respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.

However,
the Respondent No.2 being the insurer is directed to deposit the Award amount SCCH-25 and interest before this Tribunal within 60 days from the date of this Judgement.

On deposit of the award amount and interest, Rs.44,000/ shall be released to the petitioner Nos.2 & 3 and Rs.5,00,000/ shall be depsoited in the name of petitioner No.1 in any N/S Bank for a period of 3 years and remaining amount shall be released to the petitioner No.1 by way of e payment with proper identification and due acknowledgment.
The Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1000/.
Draw Award accordingly.
(Dictated to the stenographer on line, revised, corrected and then pronounced in the open court this the 15th day of April 2024.)
(PRAKRITI KALYANPUR) XXIII ASCJ, Member MACT Bangalore.
